placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 30.500, v -7.500 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom that says little away from them, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of trace on this coarser copy. Rotation 179.318 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'Second Empire' overlaid with the frontage row: The David Kelley house of 1871, Mrs. Philip D. Armour's in 1904: the register's Second Empire 'patterned slate mansard and cresting' as the family's mansard with dormers over three storeys and a stone street face, the 'central arched doorway and pediment' as a central entrance. Its quoins, paired arches and stepped stair are T-1925's. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 2347733352 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. Liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-east-2352.

built.note: The marker: 'David Kelley-Philip D. Armour Residence. Built 1871'.

Any lake edge: the sheet ends at Calumet Avenue

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2352, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1925 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 35 trace (s35fp-2115-b1), the T-1842 census (s35-2115-front, s35-2115-wing) and the T-1837 register row frontage-35-086 (Kelley/Armour Second Empire); every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-east-2352).
